reason: Attempt 3 was 75.6%. Its largest remaining confusions were transfers versus deposit accounts, cards versus deposit accounts, and loan products versus reporting. Replace the long exception-heavy classification instruction with concise positive definitions for the same ten product labels.
instruction: Select exactly one allowed label using these product definitions. Checking or savings account: maintaining a bank deposit account, its balance, access, fees, overdrafts, checks, or debit-card servicing. Credit card: a revolving card account, purchase-charge dispute, balance transfer, interest, billing, rewards, or card payment. Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports: a credit bureau or reporting service's files, inquiries, investigation, disclosure, or correction of information. Debt collection: a third-party collector, collection demand, debt validation, collection lawsuit, or garnishment. Money transfer, virtual currency, or money service: executing, receiving, reversing, tracing, or releasing a remittance, wire, electronic money transfer, payment-processing service, digital wallet, or virtual-currency transaction, including a transfer performed by a bank. Mortgage: a home-secured loan and its origination, servicing, escrow, or foreclosure. Payday loan, title loan, personal loan, or advance loan: personal or installment borrowing, cash advances, payday borrowing, or borrowing secured by an already-owned vehicle's title. Prepaid card: a gift, reloadable, stored-value, payroll, or benefit card and access to its funds. Student loan: education borrowing and its servicing. Vehicle loan or lease: financing or leasing a vehicle purchase, vehicle payments, or repossession. Choose the product responsible for the disputed service, not a different product mentioned only as a destination of funds or background context. Generic references to fraud, credit reports, legal rights, or a bank do not themselves determine the label.
